stories.headline: John Hardy Builds Momentum With Billie Eilish, Finneas and a Growing Jewelry Business

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia executes cleaners for ‘indecent act’ in Mecca
stories.claim: Saudi Arabia executed two Bangladeshi citizens for an alleged indecent act in a Mecca mosque, drawing anger in Bangladesh.
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia executed two Bangladeshi citizens, Suety Akter and Nazrul Islam, on 14 October for an alleged indecent act inside a Mecca mosque, under a discretionary ta'zir sentence. Bangladesh only learned of the executions afterwards, and the victims' families dispute the kingdom's account and say they were not informed. Bangladesh has requested a full account, but Riyadh has not yet responded. The case comes as Britain deepens its military support for Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks, with RAF Typhoon jets being sent for defensive missions. Rights groups say Saudi executions hit a record last year.

stories.headline: My dying daughter gasped in pain while medics argued at her bedside

The attempt was spotted in a honeypot, a deliberately vulnerable server, and came from an IP address linked to an anonymisation network. AWS says several attempts were made in the hours before the 10 am ET disclosure, likely by multiple actors, and that the bugs are now being widely exploited. It is unclear how the attacker obtained exploit information before disclosure. AWS argues that AI-assisted analysis is shortening the time between a patch and a working exploit, which may force faster coordinated disclosure. The PHP Foundation had not responded to comment requests.

stories.summary: Rio Tinto and California-based Rondo Energy have started engineering and design work on a heat battery at Rio Tinto's Yarwun alumina refinery near Gladstone, Queensland. The system would store cheap midday electricity in refractory bricks and release it as steam after dark. Rio Tinto estimates it could supply around 5% of the refinery's steam needs and cut direct emissions by about 67,000 tonnes of CO2 a year. The Australian Renewable Energy Agency is providing A$3.6 million for the study, with up to A$38 million for deployment if the project proceeds. A feasibility study is expected to take about 12 months.
key_points: Rio Tinto and Rondo Energy have begun engineering and design work on a heat battery at Yarwun, Queensland.
The system would store electricity as heat in bricks and produce steam for the refinery.

stories.market_take: Mostly a study-stage emissions project; little near-term financial effect on Rio Tinto.

stories.headline: Solana’s Alpenglow, its biggest network overhaul since 2020, goes live Wednesday
stories.claim: Solana's Alpenglow upgrade, its biggest overhaul since 2020, switches on Wednesday to cut settlement time sharply.
stories.summary: CoinDesk reports that Solana's Alpenglow upgrade goes live on Wednesday, aiming to make transactions irreversible in about 150 milliseconds, down from roughly six seconds. The upgrade moves voting off the chain and bundles votes into certificates that lock in transactions in one or two rounds. Validators would pay a flat admission ticket of 0.8 SOL per epoch instead of vote fees, which the article says is about 60% cheaper. The test network was restarted six times since May and one migration was rolled back before a later one succeeded. The switch takes effect at epoch 1064.

Police seized 228 camping structures, and protesters voted to re-establish the Lisbon tent camp. Similar protests are occurring in Spain, France, Belgium and Italy.

stories.headline: Italy approves sweeping security measures in response to protests
stories.claim: Italy's cabinet approved 500 troops for Milan and tougher protest penalties after weekend cost-of-living unrest.
stories.summary: Italy's cabinet approved sending 500 troops to Milan and new legal measures after cost-of-living protests turned violent in northern cities at the weekend. The new offence covers taking part in a group of at least five people who endanger public safety, with up to five years in prison and fines of up to €20,000. Parents can be held liable for vandalism by minors, and police can detain 14 to 17-year-olds who pose a danger. The cabinet did not approve giving soldiers policing powers, after opposition from President Mattarella. Protests were driven by fuel and energy prices, rents and wages, and a separate lorry-driver protest in the south is disrupting supply chains. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni faces pressure ahead of the 2027 elections.

stories.claim: US utilities are demanding stricter terms from data centre developers to filter out speculative projects, as much planned capacity is delayed or cancelled.
stories.summary: Citing a Wall Street Journal report and Wood Mackenzie analysis, US utilities are imposing higher rates, longer contracts, collateral and study fees on data centre developers to weed out speculative 'phantom' projects. Developers have requested 1,066GW of grid connections, roughly 83% of US utility-scale capacity at the end of 2025, but Wood Mackenzie expects only about 28% to be served. Exelon's high-probability data centre load reportedly fell nearly 40% after it introduced stricter agreements. PJM capacity prices have hit the cap, and households face rising bills in some areas. Average minimum contract lengths for large customers have risen to about 10.8 years.

stories.headline: Anthropic pitches AI safety bill that may block a model if 50+ people could be killed
stories.claim: Anthropic has circulated a draft US AI safety bill that would let courts block model releases posing catastrophic risk.
stories.summary: According to Politico, Anthropic has been promoting a draft AI safety bill to Congress. The bill would allow a release to be blocked where there is a foreseeable, imminent risk of over 50 deaths or over $1 billion in property damage, tied to biological weapons, loss of developer control, or cyberattacks. Independent evaluators registered with the Commerce Department would flag risks, which would then need a federal judge to halt a release, and no agency could block a model on its own. The spokesperson confirmed the draft and linked it to the company's Advanced AI Framework. The thresholds resemble those in California's recently passed SB 53.
key_points: Anthropic has shared a draft AI safety bill with lawmakers, as reported by Politico.
The bill would allow blocking a model release where there is an imminent risk of 50+ deaths or $1bn+ damage.
Independent evaluators registered with the Commerce Department would raise the alarm within 72 hours.
A federal judge, rather than an agency, would decide whether to halt a release.
The thresholds mirror California's SB 53, and Anthropic says the bill reflects its advocacy since June.
stories.market_take: Mainly a policy signal for AI labs; limited direct effect on listed stocks at this stage.

It plans to land on Phobos up to twice in 2029, collect at least 10 grams of material, and send a return capsule to South Australia in 2031. The mission carries contributions from NASA, France and Germany, and US researchers will receive 15 percent of the samples. Officials describe it as the first sample return from the Martian moons.

stories.summary: Espoo-based Coherence Quantum, a startup spun out of Aalto University, has raised €2.78 million in seed funding led by Lifeline Ventures, with participation from Mårten Mickos. The company is developing technology to reduce the wiring and heat load that comes with controlling quantum processors as they scale. Its CEO, Aashish Sah, said scaling from a thousand to thousands of qubits would need at least 3,000 control lines, beyond what standard dilution fridges can accommodate. The company holds four patent applications, and its approach focuses on filters and components placed close to the qubit to reduce heat and noise.
key_points: Coherence Quantum raised €2.78 million in seed funding led by Lifeline Ventures.
Mårten Mickos, former MySQL CEO, also participated in the round.
The company is working on control technology for superconducting and spin qubits.
CEO Aashish Sah said standard fridges fit about a thousand control lines, creating a bottleneck.
The startup has four patent applications, including components claimed to cut heat-induced disturbance by a factor of 100.

stories.headline: Hollywood AI-listers: is the technology ready to rival flesh-and-blood film stars?

Framestore's Tim Webber is sceptical that AI can capture genuine human emotion, while AI filmmakers argue the technology is transforming production. The piece also describes the labour-intensive prompting process needed to get convincing performances.

stories.headline: Deadly fire at Canada military base moved a kilometre 'in 30 to 60 seconds'
stories.claim: A fire at CFB Wainwright in Alberta killed four Canadian soldiers and injured dozens during live-fire training.
stories.summary: A fire broke out on Saturday at a grassy training area at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta, spreading rapidly in strong winds. Four members of the Canadian military died, and 39 injured people are in hospital, at least 19 of them critically. Commander Maj-Gen Wade Rutland said the fire moved a kilometre in 30 to 60 seconds after the wind shifted, and that training had continued for some hours after the fire was known. Officials have ruled out terrorism, and say the cause is not yet known and an investigation may take at least a month. Prime Minister Mark Carney called it one of the worst peacetime tragedies for Canada's forces.
key_points: Four Canadian military members died and 39 people are in hospital, at least 19 in critical condition.
The fire began around 16:00 local time on Saturday during live-munitions training.

stories.headline: Alberta heads to polls to decide whether to hold vote on separation from Canada
stories.claim: Alberta votes on whether to hold a future binding referendum on separating from Canada, with results expected early Tuesday.
stories.summary: Voters in Alberta are going to the polls to decide whether the province should hold a binding referendum on separating from Canada at a later date, possibly as early as 2027. The vote was called by Premier Danielle Smith after a pro-separation petition gathered about 300,000 signatures, though a court has blocked that petition over inadequate consultation with First Nations. Polls suggest most Albertans favour remaining in Canada, and early voting turnout appears strong. Prime Minister Mark Carney has urged a decisive vote against separation, while Albertans will also vote on nine other questions, several on immigration control. Hand counting begins no earlier than 20:00 local time and results are expected in the early hours of Tuesday.
key_points: Albertans vote on whether to start the legal process toward a binding separation referendum.
Premier Danielle Smith opposes separation but allowed the vote after a grassroots petition.

Polls suggest a majority would vote to remain in Canada; early turnout appears strong.

stories.market_take: A vote for separation could weigh on Canadian dollar and energy-linked assets, though the outcome is widely expected to favour remaining in Canada.
